analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | systemic ... 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: The desk says the 10/22 move was broad and not about Q3 earnings details. It cannot say why it started today or whether it continues, and notes clients repositioning, more around AI than normal.
Earnings winners on 10/22 were CSX, UNP, URI and LMT. Losers were BMI, ALLE, ROP, ROL, R, TSCO, POOL, CRS, HXL, MSM and WCN, so the earnings reactions were mismatched across names.
Knock-on pain is flagged in ATI, PH, HWM and WSO, in housing-related names, in many AI-linked names and in many non-AI names such as software.
Factor moves were multiple standard deviations across many factors. Short interest, profitability and value were higher, high-beta momentum was down and residual volatility was lower.
Unconstrained Momentum (GSPRHIMO) is having its worst drawdown since the GFC, excluding the Covid period.
GS Prime Book data as of October 19, 2026 shows it reducing exposure to Momentum and increasing exposure to Profitability.

FIX reports after the close on 10/22 and the desk calls the setup tough. FIX is central to the AI/data center beat-and-raise group and E&Cs have become more crowded within AI-touching industrials. It is up 50% YTD and about 40% after the day's drop, so the bar is not low. Beat, raise and strong book-to-bill are all expected, and the desk says it needs a pristine print to grind higher. Technical levels are higher and it has broken well below the 200-day.

On rates, the desk has flagged that relief in rates, from lower inflation expectations or growth fears, would move subsectors that are not owned and likely heavily shorted. It believes growth fears are driving rates lower on 10/22 and sparking the reaction.

Crude is higher, which the desk says is as troublesome as the rate move. Inflation fears are persistent if not accelerating, which brings in stagflation concerns. The desk says it has a basket for that.
The desk asks where housing can go and answers higher.
